A product consists of three components produced by four workshops, each with a limited number of production hours. Table 1.4 below provides the production rates of the three components. The objective is to determine the number of hours each workshop should allocate to each component to maximize the number of completed products. Formulate this problem as a linear programming problem.

Table 1.4

| Workshop | Production Capacity (hours) | Production Rate (units/hour) |   |   |
| :------: | :-------------------------: | :--------------------------: | - | - |
|          |                             | Component 1 | Component 2  | Component 3 |
|    A     |           100               |      10      |      15     |      5      |
|    B     |           150               |      15      |      10     |      5      |
|    C     |           80                |      20      |      5      |      10     |
|    D     |           200               |      10      |      15     |      20     |

Robust Extension:
In this robust version, certain parameters in the problem are treated as uncertain — they are not fixed at their nominal values. Instead, each uncertain parameter is modeled as its nominal value plus a perturbation, and it is this perturbation that is confined within specified uncertainty sets. The goal is to find a decision plan that remains feasible and near-optimal under all possible realizations of these uncertain parameters (the worst-case guarantee).

The following parameters are subject to uncertainty:

• The production rate (components per hour) of each workshop for component 1 may vary due to worker skill and machine wear. The perturbations ξ are confined to a polyhedral uncertainty set with each perturbation ξ_i bounded within [-13.75, 13.75], and satisfying the following 3 linear constraint(s): (1) 9.2·ξ_2 - 5.3·ξ_3 + 10.8·ξ_4 = -10.82  (2) -8.5·ξ_2 + 1.5·ξ_3 - 4.1·ξ_4 ≤ 127.19  (3) -8.7·ξ_1 + 7.9·ξ_2 - 7.4·ξ_4 ≥ 11.88.

• The production rate for component 2 across workshops is subject to equipment variability. The perturbations ξ are confined to a polyhedral uncertainty set with each perturbation ξ_i bounded within [0.0, 11.25], and satisfying the following 3 linear constraint(s): (1) 8.2·ξ_2 + 8.4·ξ_4 ≥ 56.43  (2) -11.0·ξ_2 - 1.3·ξ_3 ≤ 75.11  (3) ξ_1 - 8.1·ξ_4 = -78.37.

• The production rate for component 3 may fluctuate due to process complexity. Each coefficient may deviate by at most ±[0.2864, 0.2864, 0.5728, 1.1456] from its nominal value. However, to avoid an overly pessimistic model, the total simultaneous perturbation is bounded: the sum of normalized deviations (∑|ξⱼ|/dⱼ) across all 4 uncertain coefficients must not exceed Γ = 2.4056. This reflects the practical observation that it is unlikely for all parameters to simultaneously reach their worst-case values.

The robust model seeks a decision that guarantees maximizing the objective value under all worst-case realizations within the uncertainty sets above.
